raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
### What does this PR do?

Adds explicit packed-sequence `cu_seqlens` support to the Megatron backend so THD/remove-padding forwards can preserve sequence boundaries inside packed nested rows instead of treating each row as one attention segment.

This is not duplicating an existing PR. I searched open PRs for Megatron packing work:
- https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+megatron+cu_seqlens+packing
- https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+megatron+sequence+packing

AI assistance was used to help implement and validate this change; the changes were reviewed before submission.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs. Paste at least one query link here: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+megatron+cu_seqlens+packing
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}` (This will be checked by the CI)
  - `{modules}` include `fsdp`, `megatron`, `veomni`, `sglang`, `vllm`, `rollout`, `trainer`, `ci`, `training_utils`, `recipe`, `hardware`, `deployment`, `ray`, `worker`, `single_controller`, `misc`, `perf`, `model`, `algo`, `env`, `tool`, `ckpt`, `doc`, `data`, `cfg`, `reward`, `fully_async`, `one_step_off`
  - If this PR involves multiple modules, separate them with `,` like `[megatron, fsdp, doc]`
  - `{type}` is in `feat`, `fix`, `refactor`, `chore`, `test`
  - If this PR breaks any API (CLI arguments, config, function signature, etc.), add `[BREAKING]` to the beginning of the title.
  - Example: `[BREAKING][fsdp, megatron] feat: dynamic batching`

### Test

- `pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure --color=always` — passed.
- End-to-end pod run on `training-platform-agent/jkolehma-verl` using real `openai/gsm8k`, real `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, Megatron TP=2, `ROLLOUT_N=4`, 100 training steps — passed.
  - Final `critic/rewards/mean`: `0.4375`
  - Final `training/rollout_actor_probs_pearson_corr`: `0.999240517616272`
  - Reward average rose from `0.003125` over steps 1–20 to `0.342187` over steps 81–100.

![Qwen3-0.6B Megatron packing reward curve](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kolehma8/verl/pr-assets-mcore-packing-reward/reward_mean_100step_n4.png)

No-packing ablation on the same setup (`actor/ref megatron.use_remove_padding=False`, 100 steps, `ROLLOUT_N=4`) also passed. Comparing logged `timing_s/step` over steps 2-100:

| Mode | Avg step time | Median step time | Avg step time / 1k tokens | Avg reward (steps 81-100) | Avg Pearson |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Packing (THD) | 5.531s | 5.501s | 0.520s | 0.3422 | 0.999184 |
| No packing (BSHD) | 5.562s | 5.536s | 0.530s | 0.4109 | 0.999140 |

Packing was ~`1.005x` faster by average step wall time and ~`1.020x` faster normalized per 1k tokens in this small-model smoke benchmark.

![Megatron packing vs no-packing step time](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kolehma8/verl/pr-assets-mcore-packing-reward/packing_vs_no_packing_step_time.png)

### API and Usage Example

```bash
bash examples/grpo_trainer/run_qwen3_0_6b_packing_megatron.sh \
  MODEL_PATH=Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \
  TP=2 \
  ROLLOUT_N=4
```

For custom packed data, pass `cu_seqlens` in the Megatron batch metadata while keeping the THD path enabled via `actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.use_remove_padding=True`.

### Design & Code Changes

- Adds optional packed `cu_seqlens` plumbing from `MegatronEngineWithLMHead.prepare_model_inputs` through fused, non-fused, and value-model Megatron forwards.
- Extends `preprocess_thd_engine` to accept flat or per-row padded packed boundaries, map them onto Verl's aligned THD buffer, and pass those boundaries into `PackedSeqParams`.
- Keeps row-level padded offsets for postprocessing back to nested tensors.
- Rolls labels/positions within packed sequence boundaries so label preparation does not cross document/sample segments.
- Adds regression tests for flat `cu_seqlens`, per-row padded `cu_seqlens`, packed-boundary label rolling, and invalid missing row boundaries.
- Adds a small GRPO Megatron packing example with rollout-vs-actor Pearson logging enabled.

### Checklist Before Submitting

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Please check all the following items before requesting a review, otherwise the reviewer might deprioritize this PR for review.

- [x] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Apply [pre-commit checks](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#code-linting-and-formatting): `pre-commit install && pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure --color=always`
- [ ] Add / Update [the documentation](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/tree/main/docs).
- [x] Add unit or end-to-end test(s) to [the CI workflow](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/tree/main/.github/workflows) to cover all the code. If not feasible, explain why: added unit coverage in `tests/utils/test_megatron_bshd_preprocess.py` and validated with an end-to-end Megatron run.
- [ ] Once your PR is ready for CI, send a message in [the `ci-request` channel](https://verl-project.slack.com/archives/C091TCESWB1) in [the `verl` Slack workspace](https://join.slack.com/t/verl-project/shared_invite/zt-3855yhg8g-CTkqXu~hKojPCmo7k_yXTQ). (If not accessible, please try [the Feishu group (飞书群)](https://applink.larkoffice.com/client/chat/chatter/add_by_link?link_token=772jd4f1-cd91-441e-a820-498c6614126a).)
- [ ] If your PR is related to the `recipe` submodule, please also update the reference to the submodule commit via `git submodule update --remote` or `cd recipe && git pull origin main`.

Hi @kolehma8 , why do we need a standalone argument `cu_seqlens` ?

> Hi @kolehma8 , why do we need a standalone argument `cu_seqlens` ?

Hi @ISEEKYAN , the `cu_seqlens` argument contains the sample offsets in the packed sequence required for the attention part. HuggingFace computes this internally for some some models, but my understanding is that you need to pass it explicitly in Megatron. There is a discussion in HuggingFace to deprecate the implicit derivation of the packing offsets and also switch to explicit input arguments: https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/issues/46851

> > Hi @kolehma8 , why do we need a standalone argument `cu_seqlens` ?
>

HuggingFace computes this internally for some some models, but my understanding is that you need to pass it explicitly in Megatron. There is a discussion in HuggingFace to deprecate the implicit derivation of the packing offsets and also switch to explicit input arguments: [huggingface/transformers#46851](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/issues/46851)

but without this PR, we already have a method to calculate a correct `cu_seqlens` for megatron if we want to use the THD data format. And the data is passed by a nested tensor which provides enough data for us to induce the `cu_seqlens`. I do not understand why we need to explicitly add this argument because it cannot provide more information.

HuggingFace computes this internally for some some models, but my understanding is that you need to pass it explicitly in Megatron. There is a discussion in HuggingFace to deprecate the implicit derivation of the packing offsets and also switch to explicit input arguments: [huggingface/transformers#46851](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/issues/46851)
> 
> but without this PR, we already have a method to calculate a correct `cu_seqlens` for megatron if we want to use the THD data format. And the data is passed by a nested tensor which provides enough data for us to induce the `cu_seqlens`. I do not understand why we need to explicitly add this argument because it cannot provide more information.

If I understood the existing code correctly, it uses the `cu_seqlens` for padding purposes but does not pack the samples. Hence, the packing that is already supported for FSDP was not working with the Megatron backend. The aim of this PR is to enable this for increased performance.

I also included a small ablation on the effect of packing in the GSM8K example. The packing mainly helps when there is large discrepancy in the sequence lengths of the training batch (e.g. lot of padding). For GSM8K this is fairly low so the gains are modest.

We already support megatron THD format (sequence packing without padding) forward.

+    torch.testing.assert_close(restored_rows[0].squeeze(-1), torch.arange(5, dtype=torch.float32))
+    torch.testing.assert_close(restored_rows[1].squeeze(-1), torch.arange(8, 11, dtype=torch.float32))

+

+    mcore_util = _load_mcore_util_with_stubbed_megatron(monkeypatch, tp_size=4)

Hi @kolehma8 , why do we need a standalone argument `cu_seqlens` ?

> Hi @kolehma8 , why do we need a standalone argument `cu_seqlens` ?

Hi @ISEEKYAN , the `cu_seqlens` argument contains the sample offsets in the packed sequence required for the attention part. HuggingFace computes this internally for some some models, but my understanding is that you need to pass it explicitly in Megatron. There is a discussion in HuggingFace to deprecate the implicit derivation of the packing offsets and also switch to explicit input arguments: https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/issues/46851

> > Hi @kolehma8 , why do we need a standalone argument `cu_seqlens` ?
> 
> Hi @ISEEKYAN , the `cu_seqlens` argument contains the sample offsets in the packed sequence required for the attention part. HuggingFace computes this internally for some some models, but my understanding is that you need to pass it explicitly in Megatron. There is a discussion in HuggingFace to deprecate the implicit derivation of the packing offsets and also switch to explicit input arguments: [huggingface/transformers#46851](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/issues/46851)

but without this PR, we already have a method to calculate a correct `cu_seqlens` for megatron if we want to use the THD data format. And the data is passed by a nested tensor which provides enough data for us to induce the `cu_seqlens`. I do not understand why we need to explicitly add this argument because it cannot provide more information.

> 
> but without this PR, we already have a method to calculate a correct `cu_seqlens` for megatron if we want to use the THD data format. And the data is passed by a nested tensor which provides enough data for us to induce the `cu_seqlens`. I do not understand why we need to explicitly add this argument because it cannot provide more information.

If I understood the existing code correctly, it uses the `cu_seqlens` for padding purposes but does not pack the samples. Hence, the packing that is already supported for FSDP was not working with the Megatron backend. The aim of this PR is to enable this for increased performance.

I also included a small ablation on the effect of packing in the GSM8K example. The packing mainly helps when there is large discrepancy in the sequence lengths of the training batch (e.g. lot of padding). For GSM8K this is fairly low so the gains are modest.

We already support megatron THD format (sequence packing without padding) forward.
https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/verl/models/mcore/model_forward.py#L74-L125
